item.title: Unitarity of CFT
item.description: In CFT, we are working on infinite dimensional representations of the conformal group, as this group is not compact and therefore can’t admit finite unitary representations.

item.title: Generalized Free Theories
item.description: Free theories Consider the simplest free CFT: \mathcal{L} = -\frac{1}{2}\phi \square\phi where \phi is a primary operator whose dimension is \Delta _\phi = \frac{d-2}{2}, which implies that the theory has a unitary representation in Minkowskian signature.

item.title: Operator Product Expansion
item.description: The Operator Product Expansion (OPE) is a technique used in CFT inside a correlator to expand the product of two operators into a convergent sum of local operators applied to primaries.

item.title: Quantization in conformal symmetry
item.description: Usually, when we quantize a theory, we select a direction of time and identify manifolds which are always orthogonal to the time direction (so they are space-like, admitting delta t =0) where we perform the quantization.

item.title: Reflection positivity
item.description: Reflection positivity means that a theory, whose observables are O_i(x_i), given a reflection transformation \Theta, satisfy: \corr{O_1(x_1)...O_n(x_n)\Theta(O_1(x_1))...\Theta(O_n(x_n))}>0 The operator \Theta can be whatever, an example can be a reflection along an axis.
